title: 2009 AMC 10B Problem 8
statement: In a certain year the price of gasoline rose by \(20\%\) during January, fell by \(20\%\) during February, rose by \(25\%\) during March, and fell by \(x\%\) during April. The price of gasoline at the end of April was the same as it had been at the beginning of January. To the nearest integer, what is \(x?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(p\) be the starting price. After March the price is \[ (1.2)(0.8)(1.25)p=1.2p. \] The April drop must return it to \(p,\) so it removes \(0.2p,\) a fraction \[ x=100\cdot\dfrac{0.2p}{1.2p}=\dfrac{100}{6}\approx16.7. \]

To the nearest integer, \(x=17.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: After March the price is \((1.2)(0.8)(1.25)\) times the starting price
April must divide out a factor of \(1.2\)
